rejected.title: Working out new words
card: Context clues
The words around an unfamiliar word often hint at its meaning. Look for a definition, a reason, an example or a word with the opposite meaning nearby.
Word parts
Many words are built from parts. A prefix comes at the start, a root carries the main meaning, and a suffix comes at the end.
Example
In the word unhappy, the prefix un- means not, and the root is happy. So unhappy means not happy.
Check
Put your guess in place of the new word and reread the sentence. If it makes sense, your guess is probably close. A dictionary can confirm it.
rejected.remember: Use the sentence around a word and the word's parts to work out what it means, then check that the guess fits.

a.q: Which part of the word "unsafe" tells you it means "not safe"?
a.why: The prefix un- comes at the start and means not, so unsafe means not safe. The root safe carries the main meaning, but it does not add the idea of not.
a.clue: Look at the start of the word.

b.q: Mia read: "The path was treacherous, so Sam walked slowly." He tested each step in case he slipped. What does "treacherous" most likely mean?
b.why: Sam walks slowly and tests each step in case he slips, which hints that the path is dangerous. A pleasant path would not need such care, so that option does not fit the clues.
b.clue: What does Sam's careful walking tell you about the path?

version.title: Working out new words
card: Context clues
the words around a new word often hint at its meaning. Look nearby for a definition, an example, a reason or a word with the opposite meaning.
Word parts
many words are built from parts. A prefix comes at the start, the root carries the main meaning, and a suffix comes at the end.
Knowing common parts helps. The prefix re- means again, so rebuild means build again. The suffix -less means without, so fearless means without fear.
Use both kinds of clue, then test your guess. Put it in place of the word and reread. If the sentence still makes sense, the guess is likely close.
version.remember: Read the words around it, break it into parts, then test your guess in the sentence.

a.q: What does the word "speechless" most likely mean?
a.why: The root is speech and the suffix -less means without, so speechless means without speech. Speaking once again would need the prefix re-, which this word does not have.
a.clue: Split off the ending and think about what it means.

b.q: Read: "Unlike his gregarious sister, who chats to everyone at parties, Tom likes to sit quietly on his own." What does "gregarious" most likely mean?
opts: Talks in a very loud voice
b.why: Unlike signals a contrast with Tom, who sits quietly alone, and the detail that she chats to everyone supports it. So gregarious means enjoying company. Preferring to be alone describes Tom, not his sister.
b.clue: What does the word unlike tell you about the sister and Tom?
